report:
### Conclusion
High-quality clinical evidence indicates that saw palmetto (*Serenoa repens*) preparations **do not** improve the symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) over the longer term compared to a placebo.

### Evidence Behind the Conclusion
* **Cochrane Systematic Reviews:** An updated Cochrane systematic review analyzing placebo-controlled clinical trials concluded that *Serenoa repens* alone provides little to no benefit over placebo for men with BPH-related lower urinary tract symptoms, showing no clinically meaningful improvement over long-term follow-up (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD001423_serenoa-repens-benign-prostatic-hyperplasia).
* **Year-Long Double-Blind RCTs:** A rigorous 1-year randomized controlled trial published in *The New England Journal of Medicine* evaluated men with moderate-to-severe BPH symptoms. The trial demonstrated that saw palmetto was not superior to placebo for improving urinary symptoms or objective measures of BPH (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa053085).
* **High-Dose Trials (CAMUS Study):** The landmark CAMUS trial tested saw palmetto extract at doses up to three times the standard daily amount (up to 960 mg/day). Results confirmed that even higher doses over an extended period did not reduce BPH urinary symptoms more than placebo (https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/providers/digest/spotlight-on-saw-palmetto-science).

While smaller or earlier studies suggested modest potential benefits, large and methodologically rigorous clinical trials consistently show that saw palmetto performs no better than placebo for long-term symptom relief.
